ThingDef.label: bokka
ThingDef.description: These large reptile-like animals normally feed on the likes of cacti. If angered, however, their durable hide makes them quite difficult to kill.\n\nTheir longer back legs and strange appearance lends credence to the belief that they were engineered to live in arid environments. Why they live underground, however, is uncertain.

ThingDef.label: ossik
ThingDef.description: A large flightless bird adapted to living in very arid terrain. Bony plates across its neck defend it from predators and from the scalding heat of the open sand. Slower to anger than its wetland relatives, the ossik is prized as a mount - fast, sure-footed on loose ground, and steady under a rider even at speed.

ThingDef.label: kudda
ThingDef.description: A cactus-form creature that has evolved to roll and creep across the most arid ground on the Rim. Kuddas need almost no water, drawing what little they use from morning condensation, and depend on long unbroken sunlight to live - sustained shade kills a herd.

ThingDef.label: thurra
ThingDef.description: Bred as a bigger, stronger relative of the muffalo, the thurra is an ideal pack beast - pneumatized bones keep it strong and dense without the weight. Its carrying capacity varies with the individual, set at birth, and colonies across the Rim have bred thurras for generations chasing the perfect pack animal.

ThingDef.label: vosska
ThingDef.description: A genetic amalgamation of big-cat, shark and sand skink, bred as a ferocious hunter for desert worlds. The vosska can move through loose sand almost as easily as open ground, letting it close on prey from ambush. Dense soils are too firm for it to work through.

ThingDef.label: khorrak
ThingDef.description: A strange crustacean bred for one purpose: mineral processing. The khorrak feeds on iron compounds, chemically working them into a hardened alloy otherwise found only in asteroids. The transmutation is slow, so a khorrak needs long stretches parked among mined steel to do its work.

ThingDef.label: ommok
ThingDef.description: Despite the name, the ommok is a genetically modified creature combining cephalopod and cone-snail traits, bred as cattle for worlds too dry to support ordinary livestock. It tolerates extreme water deprivation and grazes in slow-moving herds across open sand.

ThingDef.label: ulgga
ThingDef.description: An extremely large, genetically engineered worm, armored and tusked but strangely peaceful for its size. Old records suggest it was once the worker caste of an artificial ecosystem, now running wild and self-sustaining out on the open sand.

ThingDef.label: jellypot
ThingDef.description: Named the jellypot for its ability to produce insect jelly in its large thoracic sac, this rare animal is almost exclusively found near insectoid hives. Despite being farmed much like ants do with aphids, it does not seem capable of breeding in captivity.

ThingDef.label: truffle mole
ThingDef.description: Thought to be related in some strange way to the truffle pigs of Earth, this mole has a specialized sense of smell, enabling it to find rare fungi.

ThingDef.label: great devourer
ThingDef.description: Great Devourers are armoured worms known for their unquenchable appetite. Once a Great Devourer arrives, it will proceed to gorge itself on small prey, and total ecosystem collapse is almost a certainty.\n\nLuckily, they won't attack large creatures, including humans, unless provoked. Their whole name is in fact a pun, since they are not very resilient and are easily dispatched. They have however slow regenerative capabilities.

ThingDef.label: groundrunner
ThingDef.description: A strange chimera between a bear and mole, groundrunners were used as walking heavy tools by desert prospectors when they hit rock that plasteel can't break, and for hauling large boulders their owners can't lift.\n\nDue to their domesticated origins, they are surprisingly docile and easy to tame. Their incredible strength and sharp claws allow them to break rocks with relative ease. But out here, those claws are usually reserved for ripping apart anything foolish enough to corner one.

ThingDef.label: mature fleshbeast
ThingDef.description: The unwanted result of a genetic experiment gone wrong, fleshbeasts are usually miserable, weak creatures that ooze pus and struggle to keep breathing for longer than a few days. Sometimes, however, a fleshbeast manages to survive, and even thrive - released into the wild, or simply stronger than average, growing into a pulsating, fleshy behemoth with a ravenous appetite.\n\nOut in the deep desert a mature fleshbeast will tear into anything it can catch, and rumor holds the biggest of them are cousins to something far larger sleeping under the dunes.
